name: Oracle Agentic AI Certified Foundations Associate

sections.heading: The learning source
sections.text: I prepared for this certification through Oracle's Agentic AI Foundations learning path. The goal was not simply to memorize certification material, but to understand how agentic AI systems work and how the individual pieces fit together.

sections.heading: Learning with AI
sections.text: While going through the Oracle material, I leveraged AI as a learning companion. I used ChatGPT to clarify doubts, challenge my mental models, and reason through concepts instead of treating the course material as something to memorize.

sections.heading: Understanding the agentic loop
sections.text: One of the things I actively explored was how an agent continues reasoning after a tool returns a result. I questioned how the result of one tool call becomes information available to the LLM for deciding what to do next, and used the Oracle examples and AI discussion to validate that mental model.

sections.heading: Understanding tools with LangChain
sections.text: While learning LangChain, I explored how a normal Python function can be exposed as a tool using the @tool decorator. I used AI to reason through how the function becomes identified and used within the tool-calling flow.

sections.heading: Checking my understanding
sections.text: I also used the assessments within the learning path to check my understanding as I progressed. I passed the Module 1 and Module 2 skill checks with 100%.

sections.heading: Using AI to create a mock test
sections.text: For the certification itself, I also used Google AI Mode to prepare a mock test. This gave me a way to test my understanding before attempting the actual certification rather than relying only on passive review.

sections.heading: Making it a birthday milestone
sections.text: I specifically asked my HoD for permission before my birthday because I wanted to attempt the certification and get certified on my birthday. On September 28, after returning home late from the temple visit, I completed the final setup and took the exam at night.

sections.heading: The certification attempt
sections.text: The exam had a 60-minute duration. I completed it in approximately 12 minutes and scored 88%, with a passing score of 65%. The certification was issued on September 28, 2026 — my 21st birthday.

sections.heading: What the certification means
sections.text: For me, the certification is external validation of learning, not the skill itself. The more important test is what I can actually understand, build, and apply with the knowledge I gained. This certification became one milestone in that larger learning journey.

name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Certified AI Foundations Associate

story.title: How I Took the Certification as a Cold Test

sections.heading: A different approach
sections.text: Right after earning my Agentic AI certification, I decided to take on another Oracle certification: the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Certified AI Foundations Associate. This time, I did not prepare specifically for the certification.

sections.heading: Testing what I already knew
sections.text: By this point, I had been learning Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for around 1.5 years. I wanted to find out how much of that existing knowledge could actually transfer to an OCI-focused AI certification.

sections.heading: Going in cold
sections.text: The certification learning path did not provide dedicated preparation material or a practice exam. I had 15 attempts available, so I intentionally used the first attempt as a genuine cold test rather than spending the available attempts preparing specifically for the exam.

sections.heading: What I was actually testing
sections.text: The interesting part for me was not simply whether I could pass. I wanted to see how much I could answer from existing understanding, how much came from recognizing concepts I had encountered before, and how much of that knowledge transferred to the OCI ecosystem.

sections.heading: The attempt
sections.text: The exam had a 60-minute duration. I completed it in approximately 12 minutes and 24 seconds and scored 75%, passing the certification.

sections.heading: What the score tells me — and what it does not
sections.text: A 75% result shows that my existing AI and Machine Learning knowledge was sufficient to pass this OCI-focused certification, but the score alone cannot tell me how much of the result came from deep understanding, recognition, prior exposure, or other factors. It also does not by itself establish mastery of OCI's AI services and models.

sections.heading: A self-test, not a mastery claim
sections.text: For me, this certification was a self-test of knowledge transfer rather than a claim of mastery. The more meaningful validation is still what I can understand, build, and apply with the concepts I have learned.

notes: Earned on September 29, 2026. This certification was intentionally attempted as a cold test after approximately 1.5 years of learning AI and Machine Learning.
